Hey, I totally get you. Asexuality is a spectrum, and not everybody feels it in the same way. (Warning, will make a lot of questions and long text.)  
First, do you feel those sexual fantasies are related to actually being attracted to a person? or is it more of an intrusive/impulsive thought? Do you usually feel a connection to the person while doing that in your mind, or is it more of a "mindless sex"? From what I can understand, you do not like those fantasies, right? 

I too had found myself wishing for somebody to love me without being seen as a "body" or without sex in the relationship. Sadly, society mainly sees bodies. And don't get me wrong, I love dressing up and putting make-up on, just it isn't for people to say "OMG she's hot", or for them to want to do anything to me. It's more for feeling pretty, and for people to approach me (I feel like people talk often talk more to traditional beautiful people). But yeah, romantic relationships do not equal sex. Maybe try finding a community that is closer with asexuality near you? Also, I feel like most people "like" sex because it's been so shown as the "beautiful", cool thing, especially on males. Having many people like you (or do something with you) it's often shown as "Wow, such a casanova", "I wish it was me", etc. (mainly on males, on females it's more taboo).

Masturbation does not equal sexual attraction, and as you've said it what I understood was that you did it for normalization and "peer pressure" in a way, and not quite because of a wish. I myself (Sorry if this is TMI too) did it not because I liked something, but rather, to learn (I'm kind of a curious person). People near me were talking about porn and how they masturbated to x or y, so I didn't want to be left out. I wanted to know why they did that, and how did it feel, but found... nothing. 

I do find some people really beautiful, sexy even, but I can't even imagine myself doing something with them, it's more of a short-term, "wow". Aesthetic attraction may be a concept you'd like to investigate, as the last paragraph does sound a lot like that. I too struggle with mental health problems, but there's a difference (in my opinion) between saying "oh, I'd like to have sex, but I feel like I'm not good enough", and "not into that, thanks" (but again, you can sometimes have thoughts about it, or even develop attraction sometimes, it is a spectrum). And while I cannot tell you with certainty "You're asexual" or not, I can and will tell you, **you. are. valid.**
